Task Guide:

Simulate the thermal conductivity of a Lennard-Jones (LJ) system in LAMMPS. Define a simulation box with dimensions 10×10×20 in reduced LJ units. Set the number density of the fluid to 0.6 and the initial temperature to 1.35 in LJ units. Use a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice to initialize atomic positions and assign a Lennard-Jones potential with a cutoff of 2.5σ. Create two temperature-controlled regions: a hot region at the bottom (z = 0 to 1) and a cold region at the top (z = 10 to 11). First, equilibrate the system using the NVT ensemble at 1.35 temperature for 1000 timesteps with a temperature damping factor of 0.5, then switch to the NVE ensemble while applying Langevin thermostats to the hot and cold regions to maintain temperatures at 1.70 and 1.0, respectively, using damping factor of 1.0 for both thermostats. Track the energy added and removed by the thermostats and compute the temperature difference between the regions. Run the simulation for 10,000 timesteps to establish a steady-state temperature gradient. Afterward, reset the Langevin energy accumulation and continue the simulation for an additional 20,000 timesteps while calculating the running average of the temperature difference. Divide the simulation box into bins along the z-direction and compute the temperature profile over time. Use the heat flux and steady-state temperature gradient to compute the thermal conductivity using Fourier’s law. As the final output, return the thermal conductivity in Lennard-Jones (LJ) reduced units. This is a large simulation, hence it is advisable to use multiple CPUs. Make sure all the associated files for this task (input files, log files, any other files) are in the /results/md_tutorials/13_July_2025/tool_calling/claude_35/workflow/task_7/task_7_trial_0 directory.
